guide: Open Start and type your business name and your own targets in the yellow cells: the margin per client you want, the overhead per client, the backup pay and the mileage rates.
Check Doulas, Packages and Team. They hold the agency share and hourly pay of each doula, the birth part of each package and the caps the other sheets read. A solo doula keeps one row and no split.
Write each pay line in Pay Lines: month, doula, client, basis, hours, miles, gross, agency share, pay due and, once paid, the paid amount and date. The difference and the differs check fill in.
Read Pay Run Statement before every pay run. It totals per-client pay, per-hour pay, mileage and backup pay for each person and month and checks them against what was paid.
Open Paid vs Due Differences to see the lines paid differently and the adjustment to make.
Agency Margin by Client and Margin by Doula show what the agency keeps after doula pay, mileage and overhead. A negative margin means the split loses money.
Use Capacity by Doula and Hours by Doula to see places left, on-call days and pay per hour worked. Backup Pay by Month checks stipends against the Backup Rota.
Test a new share in Split Proposals and Agency Split Proposal, and read Owner Load by Month to see what your own hours are worth.
Use the 18 tools to price a package, assign a doula, test a split, run the pay run, check mileage and decide whether to add a doula.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in.
Read the Agency Pay Dashboard and the charts every month. Check your local rules about contractor terms, records and tax with your adviser.

listing.title: Doula Business Agency Splits, Pay Runs and Capacity Excel Template: Contractor Pay Run, Margin per Client, Backup Pay
listing.headline: Know what every doula is paid and what the agency keeps
listing.description:
Run the money side of a doula agency in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-doula who also takes clients, contracted doulas paid per client or per hour with an agency split, backup doulas on a shared rota and a part-time admin, and just as useful for a solo doula who wants to see pay per hour worked and their own load.

Pay Lines records what each doula is due and what was paid, with the difference and the lines paid differently. Pay Run Statement totals per-client pay, per-hour pay, mileage and backup pay for every person and month and checks them against the paid amount. Agency Margin by Client shows revenue, doula pay, mileage and overhead for each client, and Margin by Doula shows which split leaves the agency out of pocket.

Capacity by Doula shows clients, on-call days and places left against each doula's cap for the next months, Hours by Doula shows pay per hour worked, Split Proposals tests a new agency share, Backup Pay by Month checks stipends against the rota and Owner Load by Month shows what your own hours are worth. 18 tools answer the weekly questions: a pay calculator, capacity, split proposal, pay run, owner load, losing split finder, profit by doula, per-client against per-hour pay, backup pay run, pay forecast, mileage check, new doula case, overhead check, earnings per hour, package comparison, owner against contracted margin, year-end summary and a doula scorecard. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to doulas, backup doulas, the admin, the owner-doula and the accountant.

This is part six of the Doula Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Clients appear by name, area and dates only, with no medical detail. It helps you keep track of hours, dates, money and capacity and does not promise any result. Check your local rules about contractor terms, records, insurance and tax.
